intent: Compare the top 0.1% wealth share in the United States over time with its 1920s peak level to determine whether the latest value has returned to that level.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
Does the latest top 0.1% wealth share in the United States return to its 1920s peak level?
The latest top 0.1% wealth share (18.5%) is equal to the 1920s peak reference level (18.5%), so the latest value has returned to that level.

reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: The top 0.1% wealth share in the United States falls from its 1920s peak of 24.0% in 1930 to a low of 6.0% around point_order 22, then rises to 18.5% at the latest point (point_order 37).

units.computation: Identify the 1920s peak value (24.0% at x=1930, point_order 6), the minimum value (6.0% at point_order 22), and the latest value (18.5% at point_order 37); describe the overall decline then recovery.
accept: Top 0.1% wealth share peaked at 24.0% in 1930, fell to 6.0%, and ended at 18.5%.
The series shows a long decline from the 1920s peak followed by a rise to the latest value.
reject: The top 0.1% wealth share remained constant over time.
The latest value is the maximum of the series.

units.claim: The latest top 0.1% wealth share (18.5%) is equal to the 1920s peak reference level (18.5%), so the latest value has returned to that level.

basis.entity: Top 0.1% wealth share in the United States

units.computation: Compare latest value 18.5% (point_order 37) with reference line value 18.5%; difference = 0.0 percentage points.
accept: The latest value equals the 1920s peak reference level of 18.5%.
The latest top 0.1% wealth share has returned to the 1920s peak level.
reject: The latest value is below the 1920s peak reference level.
The latest value is above the 1920s peak reference level.

optional_valid: Mention that the 1920s peak reference line is drawn at 18.5%.
Mention the absolute difference between the latest value and the reference level is 0.0 percentage points.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for the rise or fall of wealth share.
Claims about years not present in the table summary.
Claims about other countries or other wealth percentiles.
review_notes: The table summary lists the 1920s peak reference line at 18.5%, while the series maximum is 24.0% at x=1930; the comparison unit uses the supplied reference line as the 1920s peak level per the intent.
Only one panel is present, so no cross-panel comparison unit is needed.
